extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers (Emmy Noether/DFG applicants) and university research administrators/policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for DFG/Emmy Noether-style junior research group funding: what programmes expect from applicants, what universities should provide, and how selection and career-integration are judged. Focuses on independence, resources, teaching, career prospects and international aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of junior researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Researcher independence is a key issue: junior researchers should head their own independent junior research groups and work independently while being integrated into a larger research context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence is emphasised repeatedly as central to the programme’s value (e.g., ability to choose research topics, head a group, be treated on par with professors); programmes (ENP, NWO steps) are designed to foster early independent leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Very high entry requirements / selection rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: The ENP has very high entry requirements which ‘guarantee excellent young researchers’ and selection is done by reviewers unknown to applicants in a rigorous procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection by independent reviewers is presented as ensuring quality; being chosen confers a ‘seal of quality’ that aids career advancement and appointments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom to choose research topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows should have freedom to choose their research topics as part of their independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freedom of topic choice is cited as a special benefit alongside independence and cross-discipline support; programme design should allow topic freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support across all disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: Programme should support researchers from all disciplines, including the humanities as well as natural sciences and engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ENP explicitly supports all disciplines and examples show humanities scholars being funded; funders should avoid discipline bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of sufficient resources and funding flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants should provide flexible resources (e.g., extensions, ability to move funds) sufficient to run a research group and to relieve university budgets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: flexible funding, one-year extension granted, ability to take funds to a chair, five-year guarantees, and specific sums (e.g., EURYI/ Vici up to €1.25 million) used to integrate researchers into institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and clear institutional rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Universities should establish transparent, clear rules summarising regulations for young researchers (planning, supervision, support, internal funding, acquisition of teaching/management skills).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: University programmes should state planning requirements (schedule, finances, concept), supervision arrangements, available internal funding, and how teaching and management skills are acquired — this is an important first step for fairness and predictability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning reliability / career prospects (tenure-track considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programmes and universities should provide planning reliability and clear career prospects (tenure-track options or realistic competition for permanent positions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance is needed: competition phases must be long enough to select the best people, but gifted researchers also need appealing prospects. Tenure-track models can include prearranged professorships or evaluation-based offers; these should be exceptional and used to retain outstanding candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching entitlement and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows should have a right to teach (limited, e.g., about two semester credit hours) and access to teaching qualification programmes, but participation should be voluntary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmes may permit but not require teaching; universities are encouraged to offer accredited master’s programmes in higher education or other teaching qualification for fellows to gain teaching experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to compete for university positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Emmy Noether fellows should be required to compete with other applicants for university positions and be able to apply at their host university as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universities should check for likely vacancies by the end of funding and advertise positions early to allow fellows to compete; fellows should not get automatic internal appointments without competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration with host institution and collaborative structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows’ groups should be established jointly with host institutions (universities, Helmholtz centres, SFBs) and integrated into collaborative research centres or institute structures when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint establishment ensures fit with both funder programme and university/institute priorities; integration into SFBs and institutional support (space, equipment, technical staff) are cited as important for success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership and managerial skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees are expected to demonstrate and develop leadership/management skills (managing a lab, supervising doctoral students, organising teams, raising third-party funds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leadership experience gained during funding is used as evidence of readiness for professorships; programmes support training and opportunities to build managerial competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Networking, visibility and profile-raising
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs should provide networking opportunities (annual meetings, society conferences) so young researchers can introduce themselves, be observed, evaluated and raise their profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DFG-organised meetings and discipline conferences are used to expose junior researchers to hiring committees; the ‘DFG seal of approval’ is useful but visibility at meetings is a key mechanism for being evaluated by hiring institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: International advertising and open recruitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Many positions (about half for some programmes) should be announced internationally and without specification of research field or institute to attract the best candidates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open international announcements increase the candidate pool and help ensure selection of high-quality applicants across disciplines and institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of international achievement without mandatory long abroad stay
rubrics_metrics.description: Programmes may relax rigid foreign-experience requirements and recognise international publications or other networking as an alternative to multi-year stays abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action Plan in Computer Science changed prerequisites to allow international publications as proof of networking; foreign experience is valuable but not strictly mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobility and ‘homing’ measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding schemes should support mobility (including attracting nationals back home) and collaborate with other organisations to prioritise candidates with relevant host-institute ties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Polish ‘Homing’ to lure back researchers; cooperation with Max Planck giving priority to Polish postdocs at MPI; mobility funding and targeted hiring arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-step career-targeted funding design
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful national programmes may adopt staged funding phases (e.g., Veni/Vidi/Vici) with distinct expectations: early excellence, leadership of own group, and integration as a senior researcher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each phase has different eligibility windows and objectives (e.g., Veni for immediate postdocs, Vidi for postdocs leading groups, Vici for senior integration), with durations and sums designed to ensure institutional integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensating for non-linear careers
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding should compensate for career interruptions or alternative career paths (e.g., industry-to-academia shifts, family leave) that may lead to fewer publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EU ‘People’ programme explicitly avoids the term 'postdoc' and proposes measures to compensate applicants with fewer publications due to career breaks or transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project quality versus people (‘ERC vs Marie Curie’ consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funders must decide whether to prioritise project quality over individual careers (ERC emphasis) or to focus on advancing researchers’ careers (Marie Curie model).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The brochure notes debate: focusing on projects may advance careers indirectly; focusing on individuals promotes career development directly — programme designers should be aware of this trade-off.

rubrics_metrics.name: University resource commitment and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Host universities should commit resources to successful fellows (lab space, equipment, additional staff) and maintain supportive departmental structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include providing lab space, equipment (confocal microscope), lab technicians, medical assistants, and continuing limited funding after the fellowship to aid integration and reward accomplishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund portability / five-year funding guarantees
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding schemes may guarantee multi-year terms (e.g., five years) and permit portability so that funds can follow researchers if they accept a professorship elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Action Plan allowed researchers to take funds to a chair; five-year guarantees support doctoral training continuity and make positions more attractive to recruits and to their students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising and timing for vacancy planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Universities should check in a timely manner whether a vacancy in a fellow’s field will exist by the end of funding and advertise the position early.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early advertisement allows fellows to compete fairly for positions at their host institution; timely internal planning avoids losing fellows to external offers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of interdisciplinary collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Programmes (SFBs and similar) should promote interdisciplinary collaboration to focus existing expertise across a university into research concentrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborative Research Centres (SFB) are used as mechanisms for interdisciplinary work and to give young researchers the advantages of a larger research context.
